question: A team adds Claude to the middle of a workflow that already produces frequent rework, without changing anything else about it. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Claude will refuse to take part in a workflow that has not first been documented
B) The team will need a different plan tier before Claude can join an existing flow
C) Colleagues downstream will receive their work later than the old workflow gave it
D) The same faults now appear faster and in greater volume than they did before
correct_answers: D) The same faults now appear faster and in greater volume than they did before
explanations: Claude does not require a workflow to be documented before it will contribute to a step.
Plan tier is not what determines whether an existing process can be augmented, and it would not cause rework.
The likely effect is faster delivery, not slower; the problem is what is being delivered, not when.
Correct. Speeding up a broken process scales its defects. The rework was caused by the workflow's design, and inserting Claude without addressing that simply produces more of it, sooner.
